target_customer: Per the company site, manufacturers needing assembly and pick-and-place labor; per the YC launch post, clinical research sites
problem: The company site says repetitive assembly stations lack labor; the YC launch post says clinical trial sites struggle to find and schedule patients.
business_model: Per the site, robots operated by Phases and charged per working hour with no upfront capital; the earlier clinical product model is not stated
product_category: Robot arms as a service (current site); AI agents for clinical trial recruitment (YC launch post)

founders.name: Anton Zaliznyi
prior_employers: University of Toronto (robotics and AI researcher)

founders.name: Jonathan van Wersch
education: University of Bath, BEng and MEng mechanical engineering
founders.background_notes: Led the university rocket team as project manager and engineering lead per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable robot manipulation at customer stations needs perception, grasping and on-site operation; the earlier clinical agent idea would have been closer to a 2.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or hardware shown; robots as a service rivals such as Rapid Robotics and RobCo already sold per-hour models.

market_need_then: The site claims customers want robots without upfront capital; no dated demand evidence was found. Which market the company serves is itself unclear in the sources.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic dictionary word with no brand coverage found; searches mostly returned unrelated companies.

pivots.from: AI agent (Polly) for clinical trial patient recruitment, per the YC launch post
pivots.to: Robot arms as a service for assembly and pick-and-place, per the current site and YC one-liner 'AI for the physical world'
pivots.why: Not stated, and the date is unknown. Inferred only from conflicting sources.

outcome_analysis: Phases entered YC in Summer 2025 with a three person team. Sources conflict on what it builds: a YC launch post describes clinical trial recruitment agents, while the company website and YC one-liner describe physical-world robot arms sold per hour. No verified funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unknown and the apparent change of direction is unconfirmed.
notes: The YC launch post URL was seen in search results and not opened; its title says clinical trial AI agents starting in patient recruitment. Aggregator VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed in September 2025 (YC, SAV, u.ventures): single aggregator, unverified. Competitor search found robots as a service firms without founding-era dates, so the competitor list is left empty. Name origin and logo not found. Completeness pass: the 500K round (Sep 2025) rests on databases, VCBacked (pre-seed) and StartupIntros (seed, naming angels), which agree on amount and date but not stage. No press release found.
